simple.meaning: אָזַל (ʼâzal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to go away , hence, to disappear.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, Job, Proverbs, Jeremiah, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:36. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָזַל (H235).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: to go away , hence, to disappear
definitions.usage: fail, gad about, go to and fro (but in Ezekiel 27:19 the word is rendered by many 'from Uzal,' by others 'yarn'), be gone (spent).

occurrences.englishText: For Yahweh will judge his people,
Then Saul said to his servant, “But, behold, if we go, what should we bring the man? For the bread is spent in our sacks, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God. What do we have?”
As the waters fail from the sea,
“It’s no good, it’s no good,” says the buyer;
Why do you go about so much to change your ways?
